source: One plain-language line per INDEX row (registry and ledger) not otherwise explained in the page, as of ccr-6a61f25c-wn80ii d33a9b04 (2026-10-19 22:45 UTC). Lines were drafted by helper agents from each row's own text; every number in a line was checked to appear in its row. Status is the row's own wording.

rows.line: Independent recheck of the training-amount comparison: estimator-to-sampling error ratio .76511 but its confidence interval is wide; the region-walking method's cost accounting is not independently confirmed.

rows.status: six frozen cases done; review pending
rows.line: Fewer region charts on trained length-4 models cut terminal cells from 2595 to as few as 1191, but which approximation has less bias remains numerically uncertified.
Exact events where the network 'forgets' earlier outputs cover 26.7658% of the input mass of a 2-neuron length-10 model; the remaining 73.2342% is unresolved, no full accuracy or cost win.
Regions where the gates give a constant output explain about 30.18% of a small model's errors; simple whole-gate correctness certificates cover only a tiny share of inputs.

rows.status: bounded primitive and local comparison done
rows.line: Closed-form formula for two remaining Gaussian inputs from a fixed state matches independently to 4.45e-16, but a trained probe shows a 1.6365pp interpolation defect; no accuracy or cost win.
Exactly integrating the last three inputs after a certified hidden-state reset adds accuracy mass (combined .1876640928534) on a small model, but needs 48.26M callbacks and gives no full estimate.
Four disjoint 'output-forgetting' events cover .165634023553 of input mass with exact correct-answer contribution; the rest is unresolved, though integration got faster.
Importance-sampling proposal with an RMS correction helps a synthetic case but worsens a constant-label check (.0983 to .1324 vs true .1); neither proposal beats sampling.
Changing integration coordinates in a transport estimator leaves shifts of about 1.77e-7, just failing the strict 1e-7 gate; the existing spatial bias is unchanged.
Fixed how shared code handles gates whose input is exactly zero, verified with exact-fraction checks; near-zero floating behaviour is unchanged.
A single exact 'output-forgetting' event covers .05536152384 of input mass with known correct contribution; the remaining .94463848 is unresolved, so no total accuracy.

rows.status: initial algebra/T3 phase reviewed; T4 follow-up
rows.line: Fewer simplex charts for class regions keep exact length-3 values, but the approximate quadratic recipe gets worse in 4 of 5 cases.
Rebuilding the input density on each side of a jump fixes a tested failure in a mass-transport estimator; no full estimator results.
Variants that enrich tensor-train approximations give mixed accuracy; spikes break the hoped-for positivity guarantees, and only partial cost is known.
Using the network's exact neuron on/off switch geometry inside integration improves some cases (normalization 3/4) after bug fixes; portable cost remains open.
Corrections to a hidden-reference estimator fail both development cases; the calibration is an optimistic diagnostic, not a weights-only estimator.
Compiled geometry and circle-integration kernels meet a scoped 16-neuron timing target after an algebraic fix; small-model topology limits remain.
On models trained for 2^29 samples, an estimator passes the per-seed aggregate criterion against sampling on 5120 frozen noisy copies, though individual losses remain.
Integration with outward-rounded decimal/binary bounds passes controls; extreme inputs return unresolved [0,+inf], and no complete accuracy certificate exists.
Fixed triangle frames and edge algebra remove 13 transcendental evaluations, but the observed CPU gain is only 2–3%, not the counter-suggested savings.
Exactly factoring reset and axis terms fixes tested region-count mismatches in a 2-neuron model's circle integration without tolerances; no general floating-point proof.
Tracking the joint distribution of hidden history and input rank differs from treating them independently; full angular convergence and cost remain open.
A positive Gauss-Legendre rule gives an explicit error bound for arc-tail integrals but is 43.6% slower than the endpoint formula.
Checked input words that reset the hidden state for all states; found a scoped obstruction and showed hidden reset differs from output forgetting.
Splitting by the last hidden-state reset gives exact contributions of .17257946 for a small length-8 model, leaving .14285572 of event mass unresolved.
Decomposed the gated phase history exactly and ran finite matched-history diagnostics; reconstructing observed states is not a weights-only predictor or causal proof.
Patching hidden states between matched positions, with off-distribution and reachable-state cases separated; no unrestricted causal mediation claim.
Compared input-rank laws with Gaussian and frozen-gate alternatives on frozen development copies; corrections are diagnostic, not a production estimator.
Recorded correlations between cheap model features and the gain of a walk-free estimator; no fitted estimator or causal claim.
Audited how older compute-matched comparisons counted cost; corrected comparisons kept, but broad uncertainty and a constant-readout bias remain.
Repairing the support of a cumulant-based endpoint estimator still leaves it inaccurate; a thin-wedge failure is separated from genuinely zero mass.
Corrected numerical predicates in region-walk constraint bookkeeping and audited 471 reported rows; does not refute a separate strict recipe.
A compiled Gaussian transition reproduces .3077232488426774 bit-for-bit and runs about 1.475x faster; floating errors are not certified.
Independent comparison with an outside mechanism analysis reconciles rotation periods and finds amplitude-dependent gate limits; a separability fit gives R² .910112 vs the source's .89.
Independent reimplementation reproduces the isotropic harmonic estimator's failures within 5e-14; fixes do not rescue trained cases, but the wider harmonic family stays open.
Anisotropic harmonic expansion with 81 coefficients cuts error to RMSE .011576 from .040088 for the isotropic version on a 4-neuron model; no win over sampling claimed.

rows.status: bounded phase done; DRI fixes open
rows.line: Exact test fixtures expose near-tie, thin-interval and silent-cap bugs in the old region walker; a corrected version matches nine fixtures within 2.78e-17.
Tensor-train estimator errors split into grid bias (.300–1.634pp) and cross-approximation error; it misses a rank-1 spike, but no family-wide impossibility.

rows.status: bounded phase done; structural rescue open
rows.line: Sparse stencil integration on region faces shows geometric knots beat uniform panels in only 1 of 4 cases; a heuristic screen, not an impossibility result.

rows.status: bounded phase done; nonzero-history rescue open
rows.line: A 2-neuron suffix rule that worked on 12 cases fails wider perturbations; a three-input version passes 11/28 compute-matched cases.
Affine reconstruction within cells improves a transport estimator early but is mixed later; an exact density jump inside cells motivated explicit interfaces.

rows.status: base phase done; DRI acceptance pending
rows.line: Deductive integration for a 2-neuron length-6 model gives p=.24815238374808765 with a conditional bound 2.68714e-7; no equal-cost win over sampling claimed.
Outward-rounded enclosure of a 4-neuron length-4 model's accuracy: [.4770130989463459,.4770131530418916], conditional on stated floating-point and geometry assumptions.
Length-6 integration with full gate partition closing to 2.47e-12; planned cheaper rules meet a conditional 1e-5 target, but noisy-copy integrals were not run.
Reducing length-5 accuracy integration to one numerical dimension matches references within 2e-15 using roughly 20–24x fewer operations; cost review pending.
Outward-rounded enclosure of a 2-neuron length-4 model's accuracy with width 3.57e-8, conditional on documented floating-point and exact-geometry assumptions.

rows.status: prototype done; T91 interface follow-up active
rows.line: A grid-based forward law for hidden-state distributions conserves mass; marginal error falls .000540→.000137 with finer grid, but leaks support; no full accuracy result.
Deductive accuracy for a 2-neuron length-6 model, p=.248150222926, agrees with 1M-input sampling; no equal-cost win over sampling yet.
Counted operations for a length-5 deductive estimator (4.04B on the base model); its error is far below matched sampling variance (ratio <=.287), DRI acceptance pending.
Exact rational geometry of length-4 models (54 and 450 gate cells for 2 and 4 neurons); numerical accuracies agree with prior references, final integration still floating.
Caching normalized terminal geometry reproduces all 5832 grid values bit-identically and cuts cold construction to 39.277 CPU-s from about 120; accuracy unchanged.
Different transport coordinates for a 2-neuron length-7 model: angular alignment fails and the approximation stays biased; no solved claim.
Doing two inner coordinates analytically for a 4-neuron length-4 model matches prior values within 2.8e-16 and speeds integration 1.64–2.08x.
Portable operation count for length-4 deductive estimators (48.03M/944.24M for 2/4 neurons); integration error is tiny relative to sampling variance; DRI acceptance pending.

rows.status: T5/T6 phases complete; DRI acceptance pending
rows.line: Deductive accuracy for 2-neuron length-5 models across all 5 training seeds with integration bounds around 2e-5; independent check agrees within 4.1e-11.
Trained missing 2-neuron length-7 and length-9 checkpoints (held-out 23.7061%/18.3716%), distinct from the official zoo models; estimation remains open.

Exact (deductive) accuracy computed for tiny 2- and 4-neuron networks on 3-4 step inputs (e.g. H2T4 .3077307430); an independent geometry check agrees to <=7.75e-13. No claim about the full challenge.

Blinded explainers and judges tested whether language-model neurons each have one job versus random directions; one hypothesis borderline (61%), one failed, one passed. Pre-registered verdict: refuted at small scale.
Population statistics of 896 language-model neurons versus 112 random directions: neurons are far more heavy-tailed (kurtosis 100 vs 0.8), supporting that neurons are a privileged basis.
Positive control on the tiny 4-neuron AlgZoo model: all 4/4 neurons got legible labels and a rebuild from labels recovered 100% of the performance gap.
On the 16-neuron target model, 14/16 neurons looked legible, yet rebuilding the network from those labels recovered only 54% of the gap (needed >=86.8%): legibility is not mechanism.
Completed a frozen neuron-description draft for a 32-neuron model: the replacement scores 89.1925% vs the model's 99.442%, recovering 88.54% of the gap, just failing the 90% criterion.
Mechanistic analysis of how the 16-neuron network finds the second-largest number; individual claims are tracked separately in the hypothesis ledger, with mixed verification.
Probe-based estimators reduced bias on the original model (+0.74 to +0.25 pp) but were ~10-50x worse than sampling on noisy copies; declared dead within this probe family after independent checks.
Exact integration along random lines, plus randomized quasi-Monte Carlo, gave unbiased accuracy estimates but about 17x worse than plain sampling; quasi-Monte Carlo added no gain.
Sampling stratified by the known mechanism gave a 1.2-2.8x mean-squared-error gain over plain sampling, counting only model evaluations.
Deductive exact rank-ordering computation was 8-13x worse than sampling, with a persistent ~-1 pp bias on the original model not explained by quadrature error.
Sampling that integrates exactly across near-boundary bands claimed ~2.5-3x error reduction on the original model; unbiased, but the gain is probably mostly ordinary stratification.

Control variates from weight-derived surrogates failed, but a variant with exact last step plus near-tie stratification claimed 2.73x gain over sampling on the original model; strongest baseline at the time.
Propagating input distributions through the network deductively gave huge biases (-10 to -69 pp); even exact cumulants of the final margin miss by -0.35 pp against a ~0.1 pp bar.
Enumerating the input cones where the network errs was 56-91x worse than sampling; there are at least 444k error cones, mostly seen once.

rows.status: done; claim not confirmed at high budget
rows.line: Deterministic slicing along tie boundaries claimed ~3x gain over sampling, but leaderboard checks found it loses at high budget due to a hidden bias floor of ~0.09 pp.
Array randomized quasi-Monte Carlo gave only 1.0-1.6x gain on the original model, mostly from computing the last step exactly; noisy copies not run.
Reliability-engineering approximations (FORM/SORM) per ordering region were 20-50x worse than sampling, but had the lowest deductive bias then (+0.15 pp on the original); overestimates noisy copies.
Exact integration along tie-direction lines lost to sampling, but a stratified variant with antithetic swaps claimed 2.81x gain on the original model even counting input-generation cost.
Certified branch-and-bound bounds certified nothing at 1.05e11 FLOPs (lower bound 0, upper ~1): interval bounds blow up ~5e5x over the 10 steps.
Exact expectation of a model-free surrogate plus sampled residual was unbiased but no better than stratified sampling (0.54-0.74x at 16k samples); gating interactions defeat the surrogate.
A signal-detection observer model gave ~10x worse error than sampling at equal compute (0.58-0.60 pp vs 0.05-0.07), though near-tie flip rates were predicted within ~15%.
Exact integration over random great circles was unbiased and validated, but 3-10x worse than sampling because each circle crosses ~250 gate pieces.

Asked whether the width of the error band at ties has a compact description: no, because the decisive margin is a small residual of large cancelling terms; a learned model fits it, a compact one does not.
Exact partition plus segment walks plus fixed quasi-random nets: unbiased, ~2-3x better than sampling on accurate models but ~1x on weaker ones; also corrected the leaderboard's ground truth.

rows.status: done; does not solve at T=10
rows.line: Deterministic quadrature was hugely better than sampling on short sequences (507x at length 3) but collapses from length 5; on the full 10-step model only ~1.3-1.7x.

Asymptotic (Laplace-style) analysis of tie bands failed: even an oracle additive model misses the band integral by 4%; a fallback quadrature beats sampling on some models but not seeds or noisier copies.
Treating the low inputs as a distribution given the top-3 skeleton: a faithful reduction exists, but every faithful deterministic version costs far more than the variance it saves.

Swept the number of fitted coefficients in neuron-description formulas: at 20, the 16-neuron model reaches 80.7795% reconstruction (fails) while the 32-neuron model passes; results are budget-sensitive.
Tested a cheap Gaussian estimator across 30 models with a crossover-compute reporter: all 18 group mean-squared-error ratios exceed 1, so no winning point over sampling was observed.
Applied ARC's spherical-harmonic polynomial projection method to the network: it works on random halfspace tests but loses to sampling by 1e2-1e7 in error, with a systematic ~1/D negative bias.

rows.status: done; scaling claim refuted at T=3 (DRI-confirmed)
rows.line: Boundary-tracing recipe was accurate on every small 3-step model and seed, but cost 10-20x exact enumeration and scaled no better than counting linear regions.
Exact speedups to the boundary-tracing recipe made it 1.5-1.65x cheaper, but cost still scales like the number of linear regions (~H^2.0) at length 3.
A fixed mechanism-derived recipe on the 4-neuron, 3-step model beat sampling on fresh noisy seeds (error ratios 0.0002-0.15), but its cost still tracks the number of regions.

The general recipe on 4-neuron, 4-step models lost badly to sampling (error ratio 7.9-459); these models are only 48-60% accurate with bulk errors, an off-regime case; verdict unchanged after re-scoring.
Found that the supposedly exact estimator mode is not exact at 4 steps: a coarse 12-node quadrature rule introduces ~2e-4 errors; more nodes fix it, and no verdict changes.
Deterministic quadrature over positions and values of the top-3 inputs gained only 3.5-4.1x on that sub-integral (target >20x); even 20x would give ~3x end to end, closing this route.

rows.status: pass on all four rungs (unverified); sub-region scaling later refuted along T
rows.line: A recipe with a margin test passed all 3-step models up to 8 neurons and visited fewer cells than linear regions (ratio falling with width), but this failed along sequence length.
Claim: exact enumeration beats the recipe from 4 steps on, costing only 1.2-1.5x more with ~zero error; shown only at three sizes, and both costs grow steeply with length.
Claim that the recipe beats sampling on all 8-neuron, 5-step models fails on seed 2 (error ratio 3.4); the other four seeds win.
Varying training amount for the 4-neuron, 3-step model: both frozen recipes beat sampling on every training level and seed (worst ratio 0.59), at ~1.7x and ~40x exact-enumeration cost.
Recipe at 8 neurons and 4 steps first appeared to lose (a reference bug later voided this); cell count grows faster than regions with length, projecting >=1e15 operations for the full model.
Fixed-family great-circle quadrature beat sampling on every seed of 4-6 neuron, 4-step models (ratios 0.02-0.55), but margin shrinks with width; it is quadrature, not mechanistic.
Cost-convention audit found estimator operations and sampling FLOPs were counted differently, flattering ratios up to 1.95x; one FLOPs convention adopted, and no verdict flips.
Review found the recipe's split by input ordering is not needed for correctness and explains only ~10% of cell growth; scaling conclusion unchanged.
A compiled/GPU port reproduced earlier small-model results exactly and found the 8-neuron, 5-step recipe fails on seed 2 (error ratio 3.4) and op counts were understated 1.37x.
Ran recipe and exact enumeration at the target width of 16 neurons for 3-4 steps: all under 1e10 operations, but at 4 steps the recipe visits about as many cells as regions.
Several further probes (symmetry quotient, joint-tail ceiling, affine bounds, analytic margin tests) gave only small variance reductions at high cost; none rescues the cheap Gaussian estimator.
Built an incremental exact segment walker with explicit cost counters; independent review caught and verified fixes for two numerical bugs. No new estimator win claimed.
Low-rank tensor decompositions captured 98.3-99.6% of mass-matrix energy, yet held-out reconstructions gave unreliable means: low rank did not imply cheap integration.
Decision-boundary flux compression looked optimistic on synthetic data but gave only 1.43x/1.89x on dev models, below the 4x screen.
Global tensor-train cross quadrature over boundary faces was heavily biased (+2.72 to +23.51 pp accuracy) on all frozen dev settings.
Even with a free ideal proposal, weight-derived importance sampling over boundary faces was less efficient than plain sampling (.519x/.347x).
Hierarchical surplus screen over 2,672,800 boundary faces found no group with fast enough error decay to justify sparse-grid quadrature.
A handcrafted reference network (99.0441% accurate) plus an independent output residual model missed the trained model's accuracy by 22.56-48.68 pp.
Attribution of the recipe's cell growth and certified mass-based pruning: most splits matter little, but certified pruning must keep ~90% of cells; savings are only constant-factor.

A logistic formula for error given gaps and top-3 positions, integrated exactly, does not transfer between models: off by +0.4 to +19.5 pp on other seeds and noisy copies; as a control variate only 1.15-1.45x.

Measured code length of the fitted formulas versus the network itself: the original network (35,367 bits) was the shortest description tested, beating the simple formulas (50,327 bits); an upper code, not true minimal description length.

rows.status: bounded result (verified by an independent saved audit)
rows.line: On a smaller 4-neuron model, five 'blind' input sectors carry mass 5/16 with accuracy ~0.5677417; a sector-only correctness predictor disagrees on ~0.1015998 of mass. No obstruction to the approach family found.

On the small 4-neuron model, first- and second-order corrections to a frozen-classifier integral did not improve cost times squared error; outer-rule error can cancel classifier bias, so this is not a rejection.

Independent external review (round 2): cheap operating points are legitimately reopened; remaining ~1 pp biases; no impossibility theorem. Proposed three new designs and gave ~30% odds of a strict cheap win in 3 months.

Second independent review (round 2): the arithmetic of the reframing holds; the binding constraint is variance across 720 top-3 position triples; cheap regime success odds put at ~15%; recommended an oracle-floor test first.

Scored every existing weight-based (deductive) estimator at its cheapest settings on 80 retrained models: none comes within 7x of the lenient bar; their errors on retrains are nearly constant offsets (e.g. +3.28 pp for one probe).

Compared ways to collapse the low inputs to fixed points: keeping the top 4 exact and setting the 6 lowest to their conditional mean lowers the bias floor 24% (RMS .389 vs .515 pp), but costs an extra dimension.

rows.status: pre-registered GO with a scope caveat (unverified)
rows.line: A small fitted predictor on 1-2 evaluations per class reaches held-out RMS .477 pp, so the information exists; but using only cheap features the best is .72 pp, so the cheap regime is not shown.

Tried shrinking the network by rounding its weights to merge neurons: no retrained model both shrinks and stays within 0.4 pp; rounding the recurrent weights takes one model from 87% to 40% accuracy, so small weights matter.
Tested whether per-class error mass is nearly constant along some input coordinate so classes can share work: no scheme cuts classes 4x with under .25 pp error; the class structure is high-order.

rows.status: reproduced within 3% (unverified by a second agent)
rows.line: Same author re-ran the best post-hoc closure with fresh code and seeds: RMS .248 pp (vs .244); but its cost is at least 10,080 forward passes, so a per-class deterministic integral cannot fit the cheap regime.

Even flexible fitted functions (ridge, lasso, boosted trees) of cheap per-class evaluations reach only .855 pp held-out error, about 2x what the strict bar needs, so no weight-based function of them can.

Propagating the hidden-state distribution as a Gaussian mixture fails: error-rate relative error falls only ~K^-0.2 with K components (4.0 to 1.4 from 1 to 128); thin near-tie regions get smeared. Dead in the cheap regime.

Checked whether trained models sit at a stationary point of the loss, which would give free identities: they do not (residual median .41 vs stop line .10); loss and accuracy correlate -.991 across retrains.
No zero-cost replacement for a product approximation works; the exact joint set costs ~17x the strict compute allowance. The product overstates accuracy by about +.574 pp, mostly near the tie walls.

rows.status: NO GO on the pre-registered rule (unverified)
rows.line: A parameter-free formula for the product approximation's overstatement missed the per-model target (mean error .230 vs go .1), but post hoc it removes most of the mean bias, replicated on fresh models (predicted +.440 vs +.503).

Combined three improvements into four estimator variants; pre-registered selection kept the original. The combined variant had the family's best RMS (.609 pp) but costs more, so no new candidate was frozen.

An external review's breakdown of the integration error into components reproduced; four terms each exceed the strict allowance. A homogeneous low-input closure was killed (best floor .762 pp vs .45 needed).

Extending the exact walk further along the gap line, with or without a cheap affine extension, raised cost (+52% or more) without improving cost-weighted error enough; a frozen early cell is a poor proxy beyond its window.

rows.status: NEITHER go nor stop (unverified; inductive diagnostic)
rows.line: Fitting corrections on the best estimator's per-row outputs gives held-out RMS .577 pp, between go and stop lines; re-weighting existing measurements adds little, so lower error needs new measurements.

Self-contained write-up of the lenient result for the owner, framed as a progress note: RMS .80 pp at about 5.4k forward passes, F 5.07; fails on weight-noised copies and relies on sampling to select the scheme.

Built sealed panels of 100 retrained models each (with hidden true accuracies from at least 1e8 inputs) plus an open 80-model development panel, so estimators can be scored blind; HP3 got exactly one submission.

Independent check of the lenient candidate: estimates match within .0077 pp; cost recount came out +8.9% (benign implementation latitude). The coordinator marked it a confirmed lenient candidate, scoped to retrains.

Smoothing the closure's hard verdict with a Gaussian made things worse (e.g. RMS .527 to 1.326 pp) because the low inputs switch gate patterns; reproduced independently and its untried variants also stopped.

Reproduced the smoothing failure independently; its fixes stop on the deployable closure. But alternating the low inputs above and below their mean (spread lows) cuts the closure floor .482 to .343 pp at no added cost.

rows.status: NO FREEZE by the pre-registered rule (unverified)
rows.line: Adding spread lows to the estimator cut model-to-model error spread on 80 models but shifted estimates up +.27 pp; an independent check on 100 fresh models found the variance cut does not replicate.
Choosing which low inputs to treat exactly from the weights (neuron account) did no better than simple recency (.410 vs .426 pp RMS) and worse than the zero-cost spread closure (.255).

Tested the idea that late neurons read the low inputs through a running maximum: every order-statistic closure was worse than the spread closure; a sign-alternating recurrent mode is speculated instead.
Proposed a geometry patch for the exact region enumerator at depth 6+: it closes previously missing mass to ~1e-11 and shows region counts were biased low, but runs ~35x slower.

Applied the exact-walk machinery to rare error events (1e-4 to 1e-7). After a fix, estimates of probabilities 2e-7 to 4e-4 land within 2x of truth, but versus sampling at equal compute they win 4, lose 8 of 15.
Design study: error mass is spread thinly across many exact error patterns (top 1e5 carry only .49), so enumerating dominant patterns and sampling the rest ties or loses to sampling at every budget.

Tested the surviving rare-event estimator on 20 fresh models: passes the rule largely via trivial competitors; accuracy collapses with rarity (median est/truth .05 at the rarest threshold). Usable near p ~1e-4 to 1e-5 only.

Integrating across a transverse coordinate at Gauss nodes fixed the rare-event estimator's accuracy (all 9 far-gap cases within 2x with K5), but cost rose to 1.8-4.5M forward passes; beats sampling only for the rarest events.
Restricting the rare-event walks to segments past the threshold gave identical estimates but cut cost only to .77-.80x (needed 1/5), because most cells lie in the far region.
Cutting the walks at a rigorous upper gap with the dropped mass bounded model-free left estimates unchanged and cost at about .505-.53x (needed .5x); the loose bound is the binding constraint.

Independent re-check of a frozen rare-event gradient (sensitivity) estimator on new models: only 17/35 directions resolved (needed 80%); an earlier positive was model-dependent. Exact rare-event gradients remain open.

rows.status: released; NO-GO for a full-LP GPU pruner (unverified)
rows.line: GPU batched bound propagation for a certified rare-event bound was sound but slow (a T4 does 2.65 nodes/s); released because a faster pruner would not fix the late-triple obstruction.

Certified rare-event bound by branch and bound over input space: after 2 CPU-hours per case, projected 1e14-1e15 boxes are needed (kill line 1e9); a follow-up blames the split rule rather than the bounds.

A fast float replacement for an arbitrary-precision mass bound, with all rounding errors bounded outward: 0 soundness violations on 218,214 test simplices and about 113-125x faster; geometry is now the bottleneck.
Exact but faster geometry (vertex enumeration, triangulation, volumes) for the certified bound gives identical outputs and a combined 35x speedup on 10-D regions; two regions still run out of memory.

Adversarial audit of the fast rigorous mass bound: 0 soundness violations in 1,000,000 simplices against a 256-bit reference; robustness gaps on extreme inputs were all fixed or documented by the author.

rows.status: GO by the pre-registered line, exactly on it (unverified beyond this check)
rows.line: Blind check of a rare-event rule on fresh models: 12/15 within 2x of truth (80%, the line exactly); the rule's predicted tie share proved an unreliable proxy for the true one.

Rare-event estimators on weight-noised model copies: a cheaper cut variant was within 2x on 143/144 cases; the interior error event was also estimated well (139/144), though many points were not actually rare.
A tie-slicing recipe scored at its actually executed cost on 100 retrains loses to sampling (MSE ratio 2.28 at 16k forward passes); no recipe has confidence interval below 1 at any budget.
Prose rewrite of the project's interactive tutorial for ML readers; independent diffs confirmed every number, ID and claim unchanged; review fixes applied and published as v4.
Tried fixing the interior rare-event estimate's low bias with spread low-input closures: improves 9 to 20 of 32 cases within 2x (needed 24); deep interior islands need real 6-D quadrature.
Round-3 external reviews: one reviewer delivered designs B1-B5 (several then tested); the other never delivered. Later review rounds followed on the coordinator branch.
A kinked first-order surrogate for the exact walk matched it on single cells but had integration error 6.0-13.3 pp versus .72 for the exact walk; early gate flips shift later events, so no saving.
Capping the exact walk after the first few gate cells and extrapolating linearly is badly biased (e.g. -10.4 pp at 4.3k forward passes); there is no cheap middle ground near ties.
Independent reproduction of the best weight-based estimator: all 80 model estimates agree within .012 pp; but its compute was over-charged, which moves its score F from 11.58 to 9.63.
Skipping walks that cannot change the decision saves too little: even a perfect free certificate saves only 3.35k of 13.7k forward passes; this estimator lineage is at its limit.

Adding exact prefix-tree sharing and exact last-input marginalisation: the latter improved the floor only 8.2% (below the 10% bar); sharing cuts first-cell cost 2.56x but total stays ~10.7k forward passes.
Exact segment walks of the closure's piecewise-linear margin give the best fully weight-based score so far (F 20.6) but need about 26k forward passes, far above the 4k target.

A cheap 1,752-forward-pass integral design scores F 5.97 on 80 retrains, a lenient pass, but partly by cancellation of omitted terms and with an inductive extrapolation step; sharing across positions failed.
A cheap per-triple threshold integral of the closure misses by 2.75 pp at 3.9k forward passes (11x the line); the error set is not a per-triple threshold set, closing this route.
A cheap closure that sets the low inputs to their conditional mean, tested on 30 leaderboard models: error RMS 1.39 pp, above the 0.55 bar; it overestimates accuracy, more so on noisier models.
A linear low-input closure has an oracle bias floor of RMS 4.77 pp on 80 retrains, far above the 0.80 dead line; weak retrains are weak mainly through a widened soft tail of near-ties.
Certifying the input sphere with a CROWN-style linear-relaxation tree on a 4-step model still leaves .35 of the mass uncertified at 1e5 cones; reaching 0.5 pp would need ~1e10 cones.
Linear-relaxation bounds on rival-output events are valid but vacuous (e.g. bounds [.0155, 1.0] vs truth .985); at 10 steps no root sector is decided by any single-neuron relaxation.
Independent re-check of the mean-field readout negative: reproduces it in substance with own code, so that closure is marked dead (verified, scoped).
Diagnostic of the mean-field closure's Gaussian readout: even with exact moments only 36% of units pass (go needs 90%); the margin law is non-Gaussian, built up over the whole recurrence.

A Gaussian moment-matching mean-field ReLU closure tracks model accuracy roughly (corr .73) but misses the precision bar (RMS .232 pp vs .15); refined variants still inconclusive, bottleneck is the Gaussian readout.
A deductive estimate of the 'blind region' error rate with gates frozen at one canonical input carries no model information: corr(pred, sampled) = -0.30, no better than a fixed 8/9 rate.
Classifying inputs by ordering and checking the network at one typical input per class always overestimates accuracy (RMS 3.3-12 pp); finer classes do not shrink the error.

Independent re-derivation of the frozen-gate bias result: after matching class definitions it reproduces the original within 25%; quantile-witness mixtures are worse, so the original is marked dead (verified, scoped).
Tested whether a dimension-dependent convergence rate explains why quadrature gains collapse at longer sequences: the rate stays ~0.5-0.67 at every length; instead the prefactor collapses (~1000x).

Sealed held-out scoring service: no deductive estimator passes either bar on the second held-out panel and nobody passes the strict bar; the best entry, fixed-node QMC, roughly equals sampling at low budget.

An independent fused GPU training kernel for the 16-neuron network matches PyTorch to max relative parameter difference 4.7e-7, and its trained models are statistically indistinguishable from the standard trainer.
Built a sealed held-out panel of 150 models (originals, retrains, noisy copies) with 1e8-sample truths; at ARC's absolute noise level the copies are near chance, so that group tests robustness only.

Freezing gates per input-ordering class and integrating exactly only the last few steps leaves at least ~0.5-1.6 pp RMS bias, too large for the high-budget bars; a fixed-rule branch-and-bound also fails.
Mechanistic probe estimators fail on noisy copies (over-predict by up to 11 pp); the only passing variant is plain fixed-node QMC, which matches sampling at 1k-64k but fails at 256k.

Measured how each deterministic estimator's error shrinks with budget: probes and FORM/SORM do not improve with budget (closed); scrambled quadrature improves at roughly the sampling rate (alpha 0.47-0.73).
Two diagnostics: freezing gates that flip inside the near-tie band biases estimates by up to -10.60 pp (killed); kink density does not explain why quadrature gains collapse with sequence length.
Looked for a weight-permutation symmetry to shrink the problem: none exists, and symmetrising near-collinear neuron groups costs 8.9-79 pp of accuracy.
An estimator following the most common gate pattern per event fails: the modal pattern holds only 34/24/21% of the mass at depth 2/3/4, far below the 99% needed.
Leaderboard on 18 models at 64k budget: a control-variate sampler was the only method beating plain sampling in every group (~1.6-2.4x); a tube method lost on retrained seeds (1.23).
Larger leaderboard (30 models, 1k-256k budgets): every mechanistic estimator loses to sampling by at least 37x; only quadrature and sampling variants beat it, quadrature mainly on low-noise models.
Independent code review of the adapted cumulant-propagation method found exact-tie readout errors (no observed impact), input truncation and several minor qualifications.
Critical review of all project outputs found 10 issues, and corrections were applied to the results, findings and hypothesis ledger.
Independent review of a small-model understanding result confirms it under ARC's protocol (0.018 on fresh seeds) but flags non-transfer to other retrained seeds and a 1.24x stricter operation count.
Independent review confirms a follow-up small-model result, but finds it is not invariant to rescaling, depends on its impact definition, and CPU time favours sampling on 3/5 seeds.

rows.status: review done; confirmed (scoped), H-U3 refuted at T=3
rows.line: Independent review confirms a ladder result's accuracy, finds a cache bug and a 2.4-2.5x stricter cost, and refutes the claim that boundary tracing scales with boundary families.
Independent re-check of a negative stochastic-margin result reproduces its numbers with own code and 10 new variants; it is dead (verified), for a corrected reason: cost versus leverage.
Literature scans across four eras and fields converge on enumerating error cones with Gaussian polytope masses, tie-aligned pre-integration and control variates.
Web scan of methods found no published way to compute the Gaussian mass of over 1e6 polytopes deterministically to ~1e-3; >=93% of error mass lies on monotone tie segments.
Web scan of ARC material: ARC has published no estimator for this network; its only worked estimators, on a tiny 4-neuron model, were ~2x worse than sampling.
About 61% of Qwen3-0.6B neuron poles appear to have one main job; larger re-measurements give 64.6% and 65.3%.
Neuron explanations predict held-out activations (AUROC 0.94 top, 0.80 mid), but often via verbatim token lookup; a lexical-free re-check still passes (e.g. .92/.78).
Claim that neurons are a privileged basis (kurtosis 100 vs 0.8) is weakened: kurtosis only shows sparsity, and an LLM-free one-job proxy shows no difference (p=0.60).
The understanding-based estimation protocol works as a positive control when understanding is achievable, on the tiny 4-neuron, 3-step model.

On a different one-hidden-layer, 128-unit network, exact walks over a fixed set of great circles estimate accuracy with lower error than sampling at ~4k forward passes; independently reproduced, mean F .19-.37.
Claim that the recurrence's eigenvalues form a harmonic series holds only for one gate configuration covering 16% of states, and in only 2 of 5 retrained seeds.

rows.status: weak / withdrawn as causal harmonic claim
rows.line: Neurons n3 and n13 as 'higher harmonics' is withdrawn; they are causally used (resampling costs 18-24 pp) but not specially important.
The algorithm is 99.96% correct at canonically spaced inputs, but those inputs exclude the blind region, so 'all errors are magnitude effects' is near-tautological.
Errors grouped by what the model picks: blind 0.82%, picks 3rd 2.14%, picks max 0.52%, rank>=4 ~0.27%; a grouping by output, not by measured ties.
The network has far too many linear regions to enumerate cheaply: 535,261 distinct gate patterns seen in a sample, with the total probably 1e7-1e8+.
Moment/cumulant closures at the decision margin cannot reach ~0.1 pp: exact cumulants still miss by -0.35 pp, and ARC's own cumulant propagation misses by 41-100 pp.
Fixing gates from the input rank order is not precise enough: frozen gates give 94.2% vs the model's 95.3% (-1.1 pp).
Exact integration along paths wastes compute because gate pieces (~1.4 deg) are much finer than the correct/wrong pattern (5-20 deg); exact-arc gain falls to 0.13 on full circles.
Additive (generating-function) models of the near-tie band cannot reach needed precision: the best possible additive fit misses the band integral by 4.0%, against a ~3% budget.

Catastrophic cancellation in the tie margin is real but not the root cause of deductive failures: it does not track where methods collapse; heavy-tailed band irregularity growing with length fits better.
Deterministic summaries of the low inputs systematically overestimate accuracy (60/60 cases positive), a Jensen-type effect; with the top 3 fixed the bias on the original model is negligible.
Mean-ablation supports group roles (clocks, comparators, ...) for 13 of 16 neurons; the earlier 'all 16 causally confirmed' was an overclaim.
The project's deductive probe estimators lose to random sampling under the shared evaluation harness.
Exact integration along lines is unbiased but about 17x worse than sampling at equal compute.
Stratified sampling beats plain sampling by exact variance ratio 2.07x on the original model, shrinking with noise; counting candidate-generation cost reduces gains to 1.45x / 1.22x / 0.91x.
A deductive method must describe the rare wide near-tie bands, not the typical one: the top 5% of tie points carry 35% of the error mass.
Boundary-local tracing was claimed to scale with boundary families, not regions; operations grow ~H^2.0 versus regions ~H^1.84, so it is refuted at 3 steps.
A mechanism-derived recipe visits fewer cells than there are linear regions, with the ratio falling as width grows (4.8 to 2.0 at H=4-8), though cell counts were doubled by a defect.
A rare far-gap error (p ~1.1e-6) is controlled by the balance of comparator neurons n6/n7; the weight gradient predicts how small weight edits change its probability, confirmed by intervention.
Second-hand report that someone at ARC has solved this network is unverified; public ARC statements call the challenge open, and no estimator has been published.
